headings: The role of the imbalance of ANS in HF
Key benefits for patients, physicians and payers
Phase I study: BAT in HF
paragraphs: CVRx is a commercial-stage medical device company focused on developing, manufacturing, and commercializing innovative and minimally invasive neuromodulation solutions for patients with cardiovascular disease. Barostim is the first medical technology approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (the "FDA") that uses neuromodulation to improve the symptoms of patients with heart failure ("HF"). Barostim is an implantable device that delivers electrical pulses to baroreceptors located in the wall of the carotid artery to counteract decreased baroreceptor signaling, which creates an imbalance in the brain's Autonomic Nervous System ("ANS") resulting in excess neurohormones that drive HF progression. Barostim provides Baroreflex Activation Therapy ("BAT," or "Barostim Therapy"), which links the cardiovascular system to the ANS. This therapy complements the pharmaceutical neurohormonal blockade, or Guideline Directed Medical Therapy ("GDMT"), by increasing the signaling of the baroreceptors, thereby, reducing symptoms of HF. Barostim received the FDA Breakthrough Device designation and is FDA-approved for use in HF patients in the U.S. We estimate our total market opportunity using both prevalence and incidence epidemiologic models in which prevalence reflects the total number of individuals indicated for therapy at a given time, while incidence captures the annual occurrence of new cases meeting the indication. Based on these distinct models, we estimate that our prevalence-based market opportunity for HFrEF is $10.5 billion in the U.S. Using an incidence-based model, we estimate an annual market opportunity of $2.4 billion in the U.S.

HF is one of the most prevalent and devastating cardiovascular diseases. We estimate that there are approximately 64 million people worldwide suffering from HF, including approximately 6.7 million people in the U.S. HF is characterized by the heart's inability to effectively circulate blood throughout the body resulting in insufficient levels of oxygen and nourishment to various body parts. This impacts a patient's ability to function and leads to a variety of symptoms such as shortness of breath, extreme fatigue, exercise intolerance, swelling, and fluid retention that affects the patient's quality of life, both physically and emotionally. HF worsens over time due to maladaptive responses from the body's control systems, mediated by the ANS, that lead to excessive neural and hormonal activation. Autonomic activation is also a significant mechanism involved with multiple other cardiovascular diseases, such as hypertension, angina pectoris, and cardiac arrhythmia, as well as other diseases, such as chronic kidney disease.

We are currently focused on the treatment of patients with HF with reduced Ejection Fraction ("HFrEF"), which represent approximately 31% of the patients with HF. In HFrEF, the left ventricle loses its ability to contract properly, resulting in insufficient power to pump and push the necessary quantities of blood into circulation. Approximately 75% of HFrEF patients die within five years of being admitted to the hospital for HFrEF. Patients with HFrEF are typically placed on a treatment progression plan during which they are initially given GDMT to help manage symptoms, and then progress to more invasive and costly treatment options involving other implantable devices with the most severe patients often requiring Left Ventricular Assist Devices ("LVADs") or heart transplants. These other implantable devices mostly target different HFrEF patient populations, may require an invasive procedure that places hardware directly inside the heart, and are not designed to address the imbalance of the ANS that causes the disease. We believe there is a significant need and market opportunity for a safe, effective, and minimally invasive device-based treatment option for HFrEF.
We believe Barostim offers meaningful benefits for patients, physicians and payers that will continue to drive adoption of our therapy. The primary benefits include:

• Addresses significant unmet medical need. Barostim addresses a life-threatening disease for patients who failed to receive adequate benefits from existing treatments and who have no alternative treatment options. Based on this, the FDA granted Barostim a Breakthrough Device designation for HFrEF in June 2015.

• Safe and effective treatment. Our BeAT-HF pivotal trial demonstrated compelling safety and effectiveness data regarding the clinical benefits of Barostim for HFrEF. The pre-market data demonstrated safety and effectiveness leading to FDA approval, and safety and effectiveness were confirmed by the post-market data. These results showed significant improvement in the following patient-centered outcomes:

• Exercise capacity (measured by the standardized 6 Minute Hall Walk ("6MHW") distance test): Our therapy demonstrated that patients in the Barostim group were able to improve the distance they walked in a six-minute period by 56 meters and 44 meters more than patients in the control group at six months and at one year, respectively, following implant, meaning the improvement was sustained. A 25-meter improvement in walking distance is considered clinically meaningful.

• Quality of life (measured by Minnesota Living with Heart Failure ("MLWHF") questionnaire): Our therapy improved quality of life by 14-points at six months, 8-points at one year and 10-points after two years of therapy compared to patients receiving GDMT alone. Patients receiving Barostim Therapy for two years reported persistent improvement in their ability to work around the house, sleep, their sense of control, and their mobility, while feeling like less of a burden to their family or friends. A 5-point improvement in the MLWHF questionnaire is considered clinically meaningful.

• Functional status (determined by New York Heart Association ("NYHA") classification): Our therapy demonstrated the following improvements in NYHA functional status versus the control group at the specific points in time, meaning Barostim demonstrated greater and sustained improvement: at six months, 67% in the Barostim group and 37% in the control group, favoring the Barostim group by 30 percentage points; at one year, 73% in the Barostim group and 41% in the control group, favoring the Barostim group by 32 percentage points; and, at two years, 68% in the Barostim group and 41% in the control group, favoring the Barostim group by 27 percentage points.

• Freedom from All-Cause Death, LVAD, or Transplant. Patients in the Barostim group had a directionally favorable 34% reduction in all-cause death or the use of LVAD or heart transplant versus the control group.

• Improvement in Hierarchical Composite Outcomes. Based on a hierarchical composite outcomes analysis (including cardiovascular ("CV") mortality, LVAD/transplant, HF hospitalization and quality of life), the Win Ratio (defined below) was 1.26 in favor of the Barostim group.

• Implant safety. The major adverse neurological or cardiovascular system or procedure-related event ("MANCE") free rate exceeded the performance criteria of 85%, with 121 out of 125 implanted patients being event free, resulting in an event-free rate of 97% (p < 0.001; 95% 1-sided CI: 93% to 100%).

In summary, the primary safety endpoint in the pre-market phase was previously met and subsequently confirmed in the post-market phase. In the pre-market phase, all effectiveness endpoints were previously met, demonstrating 6-month improvements in 6MHW, quality of life, NYHA Class and NT-proBNP (defined below). The post-market phase effectiveness primary endpoint of CV mortality and HF hospitalization was not met. Additional post-market phase effectiveness analyses (Win Ratio, freedom from all-cause mortality) suggested a favorable effect of Barostim Therapy. The totality of the 6, 12 and 24-month data demonstrated symptomatic improvements for HF patients who are NYHA Class III or Class II (who had a recent history of Class III) despite treatment with guideline-directed therapies and who have a LVEF ≤ 35% and a NT-proBNP<1,600 pg/mL.

• Widely accepted mechanism of action. Our platform technology is based on a widely accepted mechanism of action and is designed to complement GDMT to further address the imbalance of the ANS and the consequent excess of neurohormones that cause HFrEF and other cardiovascular diseases to worsen over time.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," before deciding whether to invest in our common stock. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations and growth prospects. In such an event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations.

We have experienced significant net losses since our inception and we expect to continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future. We incurred net losses of $53.3 million and $60.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, our accumulated deficit was $590.7 million and $537.3 million, respectively. We expect to continue to incur significant sales and marketing, research and development, regulatory, and other expenses as we grow our U.S. commercial sales force and expand our marketing efforts to increase adoption of Barostim, add new features to Barostim, obtain regulatory clearances or approvals for our planned or future products and conduct clinical trials on our existing and planned or future products.

We will need to continue to generate significant additional revenue in order to achieve and sustain profitability. Even if we achieve profitability in the future, we may not be able to sustain profitability in subsequent periods. Our expected future operating losses, combined with our prior operating losses, may adversely affect the market price of our common stock and our ability to raise capital and continue operations.

We have a limited history operating as a commercial company and are highly dependent on a single product, Barostim. The failure to increase market acceptance in the U.S. for Barostim would negatively impact our business, liquidity, and results of operations.

We first commercialized Barostim in the EEA in 2012 and in the U.S. in 2020 and therefore do not have a long history operating as a commercial company. We expect substantially all of our revenue to continue to be derived from sales of Barostim for the foreseeable future, the majority of which will be generated in the U.S. Although increasing as our commercial sales grow, Barostim still has limited product and brand recognition. In addition, demand for Barostim may decline or may not continue to increase as quickly as we expect. If we are unable to achieve significant market acceptance in the U.S. for Barostim, our results of operations will be adversely affected. Because we do not yet have other products currently in development, if we are unsuccessful in commercializing Barostim or are unable to market Barostim as a result of a quality problem, failure to maintain regulatory approvals, unexpected or serious complications or other unforeseen negative effects related to Barostim or the other factors discussed in these risk factors, we would lose our main source of revenue, and our business, reputation, liquidity and results of operations will be materially and adversely affected.

We have limited commercial sales experience marketing and selling Barostim, and if we are unable to continue to maintain and grow sales and marketing capabilities, we will be unable to generate sustained and increasing product revenue.

paragraphs: In October 2025, the CMS released the final 2026 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule. This final rule includes the new Category I CPT codes for the Barostim implant and follow-up services. The rule establishes national pricing for the code series used to report procedures associated with Barostim, supporting continued access for Medicare beneficiaries. We expect the transition to Category I will eliminate the automatic denials regularly seen with Category III codes and improve prior authorization predictability to fairly pay physicians for the procedure. The final rule took effect January 1, 2026.

In November 2025, the FDA granted an IDE study designed as a prospective, multi-center, randomized controlled trial to evaluate the Barostim device's impact on all-cause mortality and HF decompensation events in an expanded population of HF patients. In January 2026, we initiated the trial, supported by CMS Category B IDE coverage. We expect to begin enrolling the trial across approximately 150 centers in the first half of
2026 and complete enrollment within five years. The trial provides for a two-year follow-up period, resulting in the expected conclusion of the trial in five to seven years.

On January 9, 2026, we entered into an Amendment to our existing Loan Agreement. Pursuant to the Amendment, the terms loans available were increased by $50.0 million, to an aggregate principal amount of up to $100.0 million, subject to our achievement of certain milestones, and the maturity date was extended to 2031. On the closing date, we borrowed an additional $10.0 million under the Loan Agreement.

On January 12, 2026, we entered into an Open Market Sale AgreementSM (the "Sale Agreement") with Jefferies LLC, as agent. Pursuant to the terms of the Sale Agreement, we may offer and sell, from time to time at our sole discretion, shares of common stock having an aggregate offering price up to $50.0 million in an "at-the-market" ("ATM") offering, to or through the agent.

paragraphs: CVRx 是一家商業階段的醫療器材公司，專注於開發、製造及商業化創新且微創的神經調節解決方案，用以治療患有心血管疾病的患者。Barostim 是美國食品藥物管理局（the "FDA"）首個核准的醫療科技，利用神經調節技術改善患有心衰竭（"HF"）患者的症狀。Barostim 是一種植入式裝置，透過電脈衝刺激頸動脈壁上的壓力感受器，以對抗壓力感受器訊號減少，造成大腦自主神經系統（"ANS"）失衡，進而產生過多神經荷爾蒙驅動心衰竭惡化的情形。Barostim 提供壓力感受器活化療法（"BAT," 或 "Barostim 療法"），將心血管系統與自主神經系統連結。此療法補充藥物神經荷爾蒙阻斷，或指南導向醫療療法（"GDMT"），透過增加壓力感受器的訊號，進而減少心衰竭的症狀。Barostim 獲得 FDA 突破性裝置指定，並已獲 FDA 核准用於美國心衰竭患者。我們使用盛行率與發病率的流行病學模型來估計總市場機會，其中盛行率反映某一時間點符合治療適應症的總人數，而發病率則捕捉每年符合適應症的新病例數。根據這些不同的模型，我們估計美國心衰竭（HFrEF）的盛行率基準市場機會為 10.5 十億美元。使用發病率基準模型，我們估計美國的年度市場機會為 2.4 十億美元。

HF 是一種最普遍且最具破壞性的心血管疾病。我們估計全球約有 64 百萬人患有 HF，包括美國約 6.7 百萬人。HF 的特徵是心臟無法有效地將血液泵送到全身，導致身體各部位的氧氣和營養不足。這會影響病患的功能能力，並導致短氣、極度疲勞、運動耐受力差、水腫和體液滯留等症狀，影響病患的生活品質，無論是身體上或情緒上。HF 隨時間推移會惡化，這是因為身體控制系統的適應性反應，透過自主神經系統（"ANS"）所中介，導致過度的神經和荷爾蒙活化。自主神經活化也是多種其他心血管疾病，如高血壓、心絞痛和心律不整，以及其它疾病，如慢性腎臟病的重要機制。

我們目前專注於治療患有 HF 伴隨射血分數降低（"HFrEF"）的病患，這類病患約佔 HF 病患的 31%。在 HFrEF 中，左心室失去正常收縮能力，導致無法有效地將足夠的血液泵入循環系統。約有 75% 的 HFrEF 病患在入院治療後五年內死亡。HFrEF 病患通常會依照治療進展計畫進行治療，在初期會給予 GDMT 來幫助控制症狀，並進而轉向更侵入性和成本更高的治療選項，涉及其他植入式裝置，最嚴重的病患往往需要左心室輔助裝置（"LVADs"）或心臟移植。這些其他植入式裝置主要針對不同的 HFrEF 病患族羣，可能需要侵入性手術將硬體直接置入心臟，且並未設計用以解決導致疾病的自主神經系統失衡問題。我們認為，對於 HFrEF 病患而言，存在著顯著的醫療需求與市場機會，需要一種安全、有效且微創的裝置治療選項。
我們認為 Barostim 對病患、醫生和支付者提供了重要的效益，這些效益將持續推動我們療法的採用。主要的效益包括：
• 解決重要的未滿足醫療需求。Barostim 解決了那些未能從現有治療方案獲得足夠效益且沒有其他治療選擇的病患的生命威脅性疾病。基於此，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）於 2015 年 6 月授予 Barostim HFrEF 的突破性裝置認定。
• 安全且有效的治療。我們的 BeAT-HF 關鍵臨牀試驗顯示了 Barostim 對 HFrEF 的臨牀效益的強大安全性與有效性數據。預市數據顯示了安全性與有效性，導致 FDA 核准，且安全性與有效性也由後市數據所確認。這些結果顯示在以下病患中心理學效益有顯著改善：
• 運動能力（透過標準化的六分鐘步行測試（"6MHW"）距離測試衡量）：我們的療法顯示，植入 Barostim 後，病患在六個月和一年後，分別比控制組病患在六分鐘內行走距離多出 56 公尺和 44 公尺，表示改善持續存在。六分鐘步行距離改善 25 公尺被認為具有臨牀意義。
• 生活品質（透過 Minnesota 心力衰竭生活品質問卷（"MLWHF"）衡量）：我們的療法在六個月後改善生活品質 14 分，一年後改善 8 分，兩年後改善 10 分，與僅接受 GDMT 的病患相比。接受 Barostim 療法兩年的病患報告表示，他們在居家活動、睡眠、對自身控制感、移動能力方面持續改善，同時感覺對家人或朋友的負擔較輕。MLWHF 問卷改善 5 分被認為具有臨牀意義。

• 功能狀態（根據紐約心臟協會（"NYHA"）分級判定）：我們的療法在特定時間點顯示出較對照組顯著改善的 NYHA 功能狀態，表示 Barostim 療法顯示出更顯著且持續的改善：在六個月時，Barostim 組有 67% 改善，對照組有 37% 改善，Barostim 組優於對照組 30 個百分點；在一年時，Barostim 組有 73% 改善，對照組有 41% 改善，Barostim 組優於對照組 32 個百分點；在兩年時，Barostim 組有 68% 改善，對照組有 41% 改善，Barostim 組優於對照組 27 個百分點。
• 免於所有原因死亡、左心室 assist 裝置（LVAD）或心臟移植。Barostim 組患者在所有原因死亡或 LVAD 使用或心臟移植方面顯示出方向性優勢，較對照組減少 34%。
• 改善層級複合結果。根據層級複合結果分析（包括心血管（"CV"）死亡、LVAD/移植、心力衰竭（HF）住院及生活品質），Win Ratio（定義如下）為 1.26，優於 Barostim 組。
• 手術安全性。主要不良神經系統或心血管系統或手術相關事件（"MANCE"）未發生率超過 85% 的表現標準，有 125 名植入患者中 121 名未發生事件，結果為事件未發生率為 97%（p < 0.001；95% 單側信賴區間：93% 至 100%）。

總結，預市階段的主要安全性終點已達成，並在後市階段確認。預市階段的所有有效性終點均已達成，顯示出 6MHW、生活品質、NYHA 分級及 NT-proBNP（定義如下）在六個月時的改善。後市階段有效性主要終點（心血管死亡及 HF 住院）未達成。後市階段的其他有效性分析（Win Ratio、免於所有原因死亡）顯示出 Barostim 療法有優勢效果。6、12 和 24 個月的總體數據顯示，對於接受指南導向療法治療且 NYHA 分級 III 或 II（有近期 III 分級病史）的心力衰竭患者，其左心室射血分數（LVEF） ≤ 35% 且 NT-proBNP < 1,600 pg/mL，顯示出症狀改善。
• 廣泛接受的作用機制。我們的平台技術基於廣泛接受的作用機制，設計用以補充 GDMT，進一步解決自主神經系統（ANS）的不平衡及導致 HFrEF 及其他心血管疾病隨時間惡化的過度神經激素問題。

paragraphs: 2025 年 10 月，CMS 發佈 2026 年 Medicare 醫師費用排定表最終版。此最終規則包含用於 Barostim 零組件及追蹤服務的新 Category I CPT 編碼。此規則為用以報告與 Barostim 有關程序的編碼系列設立國家價格，支持 Medicare 受益人持續取得相關服務。我們預期轉換至 Category I 將消除 Category III 編碼常見的自動拒絕，並提高事前審批的可預測性，以公平支付醫師執行此程序的費用。此最終規則於 2026 年 1 月 1 日生效。

2025 年 11 月，FDA 批准一項 IDE 研究，設計為前瞻性、多中心、隨機對照試驗，用以評估 Barostim 裝置對擴大 HF 病患族羣的全死因死亡率及 HF 情況惡化事件的影響。2026 年 1 月，我們啟動該試驗，並獲得 CMS Category B IDE 覆蓋。我們預期於 2026 年第一季開始於約 150 個中心招募受試者，並在五年內完成招募。該試驗包含兩年的追蹤期，預期於五至七年內完成試驗。
2026 年 1 月 9 日，我們與現有貸款協議簽訂修正案。根據修正案，貸款額度增加 50.0 百萬美元，總本金上限提高至 100.0 百萬美元，條件為達成特定里程碑，且還款期限延長至 2031 年。於簽約日，我們根據貸款協議額外取得 10.0 百萬美元貸款。
於 2026 年 1 月 9 日，本公司與現有貸款協議簽訂了修正案。根據該修正案，貸款額度增加 50.0 百萬美元，總計可達 100.0 百萬美元，條件為本公司達成特定里程碑，且到期日延長至 2031 年。於關閉日，本公司根據貸款協議額外取得 10.0 百萬美元貸款。
2026 年 1 月 12 日，我們與 Jefferies LLC 簽訂公開市場銷售協議（"Sale Agreement"），由 Jefferies LLC 作為經紀人。根據銷售協議的條款，我們可隨時根據本公司單獨判斷，以 "at-the-market"（"ATM"）方式，出售總發售價格達 50.0 百萬美元的普通股，透過或由經紀人進行銷售。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們有持續出現重大虧損的歷史，且我們預期這種情況會持續，我們可能無法實現或維持盈利。若我們無法實現並維持盈利，我們的財務狀況可能會受到影響。
我們必須向醫師及患者說明 Barostim 的優勢。
若我們無法獲得醫院的准入，我們的銷售可能會減少。
製造風險可能會不利於我們製造產品的能力，並可能降低我們的毛利率及盈利。
我們僅在一個場地運營，若此場地出現中斷，可能會對我們的業務造成影響。
我們的國際業務使我們面臨某些營運風險，這些風險可能會對我們的營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
若我們無法有效地管理成長，我們的業務可能會受到影響。
若未來適應症之臨牀研究無法產生支持美國或其他地區法規審查或核准之結果，本公司將無法針對這些適應症商業化其產品。
本公司可能面臨產品責任訴訟，此等訴訟可能造成財務負擔、分散管理階層之注意力，並損害本公司之聲譽。
若本公司無法留住關鍵高階主管或招募與聘僱新進員工，本公司之營運及財務結果可能受到不利影響，同時吸引其他具備高度資格之人才。
不利之經濟條件可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成不利影響。
若第三方支付者未為Barostim之使用提供充分之保障與報銷，本公司之營業收入將受到負面影響。
美國或全球範圍內若發生疫情、疫病或傳染病爆發，可能對本公司之業務造成不利影響。
與智慧財產權相關之風險
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。您應謹慎考慮下列所列風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括我們合併財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」，再決定是否投資本公司普通股。上述任何事件或發展之發生，可能會損害本公司聲譽、業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長前景。在這種情況下，本公司普通股市價可能會下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司認為不重要，也可能影響本公司業務營運。
我們需要持續產生重大額外收入，以實現並維持盈利。即使我們未來實現盈利，我們可能無法在隨後期間維持盈利。我們預期未來營運虧損，加上過去營運虧損，可能會不利於本公司普通股市價，以及我們籌資能力與持續營運。
我們營運作為商業公司之歷史有限，且高度依賴單一產品Barostim。若無法提高Barostim在美國之市場接受度，將會對我們業務、流動性及營運結果產生負面影響。

我們於2012年首次在EEA地區商業化Barostim，於2020年在美國商業化Barostim，因此我們並無長久營運作為商業公司之歷史。我們預期在可預見的未來， substantially all 之收入仍將來自Barostim之銷售，其中絕大多數將來自美國。儘管隨著商業銷售成長而增加，Barostim仍具有限之產品與品牌認知度。此外，Barostim之需求可能下降，或可能無法如預期般快速增加。若我們無法在美國實現Barostim之重大市場接受度，將會對我們營運結果產生不利影響。由於我們目前尚無其他產品正在開發中，若我們在商業化Barostim上失敗，或因品質問題而無法行銷Barostim，或因無法維持監管核准、出現預期之外或嚴重之問題或其他未預見之負面影響而導致Barostim之問題，或因其他在這些風險因素中所討論之因素，我們將失去主要收入來源，將對我們業務、聲譽、流動性及營運結果造成重大且不利之影響。
我們在行銷與銷售Barostim方面之商業銷售經驗有限，若我們無法持續維持並成長銷售與行銷能力，將無法產生持續且增加之產品收入。
